perspectives.title: 1. Purpose
paragraphs: Convert concerns into source-bounded questions, not votes or findings by popularity.

perspectives.title: 2. Scope
paragraphs: Eleven historical clusters, fourteen linked collections; not exhaustive community input.

perspectives.title: 3. Coverage
paragraphs: Screenshots, prompts, media, testimony and formal agency processes differ; originals not exhaustively recovered.

perspectives.title: 4. Provenance
paragraphs: Retain event/capture date, publisher, locator and exact edition; raw material stays controlled.

perspectives.title: 5. Classification
paragraphs: Separate experience, opinion, allegation, official statement, adopted action, reporting and inference.

perspectives.title: 6. Deduplication
paragraphs: Overlaps and repeated summaries do not add independent evidence.

perspectives.title: 7. Representation
paragraphs: No representative polling denominator or authenticated contributor count exists.

perspectives.title: 8. Freshness
paragraphs: Reopen when records, decisions or corrections arrive; preserve original snapshots; editorial recheck December 2.

perspectives.title: 9. Jurisdiction
paragraphs: City, County, district, state and federal authorities differ; cooperation does not confer control.

perspectives.title: 10. Delivery
paragraphs: Trace adopted vote, assigned administration, funding and completed work via S1–S3.

perspectives.title: 11. Finance
paragraphs: Distinguish request, appropriation, commitment, cash, reimbursement and audit; eliminate duplicate transfers.

perspectives.title: 12. Procurement
paragraphs: Seek solicitation, addenda, evaluation, award, change orders and acceptance; missing records do not prove misconduct.

perspectives.title: 13. Half-Cent
paragraphs: Trace eligibility, remaining cash, restricted funds, commitments and additional economic outcomes.

perspectives.title: 14. Infrastructure
paragraphs: Split pre-existing maintenance and incremental demand; assess lifecycle cost and asset condition.

perspectives.title: 15. Urban renewal
paragraphs: Follow adopted plan, adjusted base, increment, reimbursements and public benefit. [S4]

perspectives.title: 16. Jobs and training
paragraphs: Measure filled positions, actual resident hires, wage bands, credentials and retention.

perspectives.title: 17. Local business
paragraphs: Assess permitting time, access and cost without exposing confidential firm records.

perspectives.title: 18. Tourism scenario
paragraphs: 3,009,507 visits × 5% × $25 ≈ $3.76m; 15% × $40 ≈ $18.06m; 30% × $60 ≈ $54.17m illustrative gross added purchases. Excludes displacement, leakage and cost; not tax revenue or forecast.

paragraphs: Compare operating costs, condition, cultural access and alternative uses; one appraisal cannot decide public value.

perspectives.title: 20. Housing
paragraphs: Track completed and occupied homes, affordability, transport and repairs; planned unit is not occupancy.

perspectives.title: 21. Environment
paragraphs: Separate hazard, possible and measured exposure, and health outcomes. No personal exposure claims.

perspectives.title: 22. Water and drainage
paragraphs: Test runoff, maintenance and capacity against engineered requirements and measurements.

perspectives.title: 23. Health and services
paragraphs: Verify actual geography, eligibility, availability and waitlists; funding announcements are not service confirmation.

perspectives.title: 24. Public safety

paragraphs: AI summaries are leads; correct exact dated propositions with originals rather than attack speakers.

perspectives.title: 29. LL / GLEAN

perspectives.title: 30. DBL

paragraphs: Watch actual deadlines, irreversible costs and delay risks; monitoring design is not active monitoring.

perspectives.title: 36. LEAP
paragraphs: Illustrative 2027 baseline/pilot, 2029 cost/outcomes review, 2031 durability audit; not commitments.

perspectives.title: 37. T2Y
paragraphs: Compare short/long cost, rights, family impacts, alternatives, reversibility and opportunity cost.

perspectives.title: 38. Twin and Shadow
paragraphs: Link issue-level evidence, institutions, decisions and outcomes; separate observed state and scenarios. No live import or person-level graph.

sections.title: Research paper: method, findings and limitations
text: Abstract. This longitudinal, qualitative case synthesis evaluates how public questions can generate accountable research without equating online visibility with prevalence. Eleven previously recovered clusters are compared across fourteen existing editorial collections. The observational material is non-random, incomplete and sometimes duplicated. No statistical inference about Pueblo residents is warranted.

Research question. Can an evidence-controlled workflow convert a concern into a specific, independently checkable proposition, an accountable action option, and an outcome measure without compromising privacy or duplicating work? The evidence supports feasibility of the workflow at a design and offline reference level; it does not establish improvements in public outcomes.

Method. Unit of analysis: issue-level question, not individual or social account. Recover earlier artifacts; classify source family and claim type; preserve contrary editions; compare against relevant official records; route to existing issue IDs; retain unresolved questions. Treat dates of event, publication, retrieval and legal effect separately. Qualitative clustering is editorial, not a coded random sample. Original screenshots and formal submissions were not completely recovered, so intercoder reliability, prevalence and response rates cannot be calculated.

Result. The recovered crosswalk joins 11 clusters to 14 collections, retaining 4 collections with no mapping in this subset. Common structural gaps concern actual payments versus authorization, adopted action versus implementation, announcement versus delivered service, and attribution versus proof. These are recurring evidence problems, not estimates of institutional misconduct.

Counterfactual. A single unverified claim can generate multiple duplicate reports. A source return and versioned correction can avoid that duplication. Conversely, overly aggressive matching could erase genuinely independent observations or suppress adverse evidence. Keep separate original editions, review contested mappings and allow correction or appeal.

Limits. No original-byte certification, full chat census, current service outcome study or population-level poll. This paper is an editorial synthesis, not a claim of causal improvement. Published records may change; future readers should verify the controlling document.

sections.title: November 19 source refresh and decision checkpoints
text: The City reported on November 3 that its proposed 2027 amount was $490,000 and that $465,500 in 2026 County reimbursement remained outstanding at that time. The $2,203,865 application total exceeds the proposed amount by $1,713,865; the proposed amount covers about 22.2% of requests if applied wholly to that total. This is not a certified grant shortfall or paid amount. Whether reimbursement and fourth-quarter payments occurred remains unresolved. Check recommendations and adopted budget in December–January. City November 3 release.

The District's September 28 statement confirms the rejected proposal's estimated HUTF range and the routine maintenance estimate. This is the District's account, not an audit of actual expenses or a current IGA balance. Confirm latest board actions and actual work. District update.

November 11 CPR reporting describes public objections to the listing, a reported $300,000 offer and an appraisal above $1.9 million attributed to City leadership. Neither source is the deed, appraisal or executed sale contract. No final sale verified. Dated news reporting.

The EPA September 1 proposal and agency document index were checked again. The comment window stated in the announcement ended October 1. The schedule gives an estimated August–November 2026 milestone for an explanation of significant differences; an estimate does not establish issuance. No final revised level verified here. sections.title: Evaluation and implementation packet
text: Measure the process before claiming improvements: percentage of material propositions linked to originals, independent source-family count, percentage of changed claims with correction history, unresolved high-impact issues, time from first identified gap to verified response, and repeated record requests avoided. Set the denominator before each review. A missing denominator is unknown, not zero.

Compare three options: retain the current manual evidence review; use the existing offline deduplication and routing reference under human review; or integrate a controlled workflow only after privacy, access, review, rollback and outcome tests. No automated public verdict or live intake is proposed for activation here. Costs require actual staff time, infrastructure and maintenance records; no estimated savings are presented as realized savings.

Review triggers: new budget or payment evidence, board or Council action, source correction, revised agency decision, or a change in permission. Target December 2, 2026 for the next editorial check, not a scheduled monitoring promise. 2027 baseline and approved pilots, 2029 independent outcome comparison, 2031 longevity and discontinuation review are scenario milestones.
